sections.h2: Who handles Muskingum County tax bills
sections.html:
Property tax in Zanesville runs through two offices in one building, 401 Main Street. Valuation and relief applications are the auditor's job. Billing and collection belong to the treasurer. After the auditor signs off on a transfer, the recorder files the deed.

Muskingum County property tax offices
OfficeWhat it doesPhone
County AuditorAppraises real estate, takes Board of Revision complaints, handles homestead, owner-occupancy and farm-use applications(740) 455-7109
County TreasurerMails and collects tax bills, sets up delinquency payment plans, changes billing addresses(740) 455-7118
County RecorderRecords the deed after the auditor's transfer(740) 455-7107

Moving the billing address takes a written, signed change-of-address form delivered to the treasurer. Calling in will not do it. A buyer who wants bills mailed elsewhere should send the form right after closing.

sections.h2: How Muskingum County values a house
sections.html:
Each parcel gets appraised by the auditor, and the state requires a full revaluation on a six-year cycle. The latest rounds were 2018 and 2024. Average values rose 36.135 percent in 2024, a jump that came from three years of climbing sale prices.

A bigger valuation does not mean a bill that grows by the same amount. The bill comes from voter-approved levies, and the Ohio Department of Taxation turns those levies into rates. Next year's rates are not settled before the end of December. An online tax estimator on the auditor's site gives a rough preview, and the auditor's staff can explain how any single value was built.

The filing window for a formal complaint opens January 1 and closes March 31, with the complaint handed to the county auditor. Under section 5715.19, the true cutoff is March 31 or the end of first-half collection, whichever is later. If you mail it, the United States postmark is the filing date. A meter mark from a private postage machine is not.

The Board of Revision hears the case. Its members are the auditor, the treasurer and one county commissioner, or people standing in for them. You can try an informal review with the auditor beforehand. Useful evidence includes:

  • Sales of comparable homes.
  • An independent appraisal from within the past year.
  • Repair estimates for defects in the house.
  • Settlement documents from a recent purchase.
  • Income and expense statements for rentals.
  • Photographs.

With a complaint pending, the treasurer will take payment based on the lower value you claimed. If the final value lands higher, the statute lets interest build on the difference.

Two bills arrive each year, one in January or February and one in May or June, with the exact closing date printed on the bill itself. Default installment dates in section 323.12 are December 31 and June 20, though the treasurer's calendar can vary. Trust the bill in your hand.

Pay late and the penalty is 10 percent of the current tax. Get it in within ten days of the due date and it drops to 5 percent. Interest is added to older delinquencies each July 1 and to unpaid current taxes each December 1. A bill that never reached you still carries the penalty.

You can pay through the online portal, by phone at (833) 505-4134, at a lobby kiosk or at the Treasurer's Office counter. Electronic payments carry a processing fee, and the counter does not take cards.

Three programs exist, and each one starts with an application at the auditor's office.

  • Owner Occupancy Credit. Takes 2.5 percent off qualifying levies for anyone who owns the home and lives in it as a primary residence.
  • Homestead Exemption. For owners aged 65 and up and for permanently and totally disabled owners. It shields $29,000 of market value for tax year 2025, and income must come in under $41,000. A $58,000 exemption applies to disabled service members and certain surviving spouses.
  • Current Agricultural Use Valuation. Land of at least ten acres in commercial farming is taxed at soil rates. Smaller tracts can qualify with $2,500 of farm income.

Two state bills also matter. House Bill 479 is meant to add roughly $475 of Homestead savings on the bill received in 2027. House Bill 186 set up an Inflation Cap Credit on school levies for tax year 2025. The auditor can tell you how they apply to a given parcel.

The tax stays with the land. Whoever holds title on the bill date gets the full-year bill, so at closing the seller credits the buyer for the months the seller owned the house. Ask the title agent to point out that proration line before you sign.

Back taxes are a lien, and a buyer who takes the house also takes the debt, which can slow a sale or cut the price. A year after taxes are certified delinquent, the county prosecutor may start foreclosure. That adds penalties, interest and court costs and ends at a sheriff's sale. Muskingum County does not sell tax liens. An owner still living in the home can ask the treasurer for a written delinquency contract that spreads the balance over installments.

Fill out the statement of value filed with the deed with care. It asks about owner-occupancy reductions and farm-use valuation, and land that drops out of farm-use valuation can face a recoupment charge.

sections.h2: Muskingum County housing at a glance
sections.html: Muskingum County had 86,410 residents in 2020 and an estimated 87,014 for 2025. Owner-occupied homes have a median value of $182,200, and owners who carry a mortgage typically pay $1,300 a month in housing costs. Renters occupy a bit under a third of homes, so tenants in place are common in sales.

sections.h2: What to do with a new valuation
sections.html:
Open your parcel in the auditor's real estate search and read the tentative value under the Values heading. Line it up against recent sales of similar houses close by.

Still off? Two routes are open. The informal review is a talk with appraisal staff. No evidence is required, but without significant documents an adjustment is unlikely. The other route is the Board of Revision complaint, where sellers and buyers can also raise a fresh sale price.

The window shuts every March 31. If you plan to close in spring, find out whether a complaint is already pending, because its result can change the bill your buyer inherits.

The auditor has no say in whether taxes go up or down. Voters pass or reject levies, and the state combines them with each district's total value to set rates.

A cash sale will not erase the tax bill, but it removes the wait for a buyer's lender and appraisal, so the closing date is not tied to financing. Whichever way you sell, the title company asks the treasurer what is owed on the parcel. If back taxes exist, get the payoff figure early, and ask about a delinquency contract if you still occupy the home. Cash Home Buyers CA can explain what is owed and how it is paid out of the closing proceeds.

faqs.q: Who mails Muskingum County property tax bills?
faqs.a: The county treasurer, from 401 Main Street in Zanesville. One bill comes in January or February and the next in May or June.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to contest a valuation?
faqs.a: March 31. Complaints to the auditor are accepted from January 1, and state law stretches the cutoff to the end of first-half collection when that is later.
Ten percent of the tax due, reduced to five percent if payment comes within ten days after the due date. Delinquent balances also accrue interest.

faqs.q: Who covers property tax at a closing here?
faqs.a: They split it by proration. The seller credits the buyer on the closing statement for the seller's months, and the buyer pays the bill when it arrives.

faqs.q: Can the county sell a tax lien on my house?
faqs.a: No, Muskingum County does not sell tax liens. A year after certification as delinquent, though, the prosecutor can file foreclosure, which ends in a sheriff's sale.
